conviction_note: Slight long lean only: a company that has beaten revenue 7 of 8 quarters, with customer deposits up from $78M to $361M in H1, faces a Q3 bar ($1.07B) that is flat on Q2 and goes into the print down 23% in 20 sessions and about 10% today. Against that are the Jupiter/Oracle overhang, which the call will have to address, a Q2 beat-and-raise that closed -1.85%, and a tech tape down 2.75% today. So p_up is 55 on an 11% abs move (+1.1), and the findings sum to +1.1. The two measurements agree, but both are small next to the 10% straddle.

positioning_check: Short interest 20.98M shares, 7.34% of float, 1.0 days to cover, record date 2026-09-30 (FINRA report published 2026-10-09), up 10.5% on the prior report: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/BE/short-interest/. This is not a crowded short. Baseline: event straddle 10.16%, ATM IV 172%, 25d skew +2.06 vol points (mild downside paid), put/call OI 0.82. Run-up: -11.1% over 5 days, -22.7% over 20 days, -38.5% from the 52-week high. Intraday on 10-22 the stock is down about 9-11% (24/7 Wall St, 13:07 ET), giving back a +7% move on 10-21 in a broad tech selloff (Nasdaq 100 -2.75%).

findings.finding: Q3 revenue bar of ~$1.07B is flat on Q2's $1,065M, though Q2 grew 42% q/q and the company has beaten revenue in 7 of the last 8 quarters. The Q2 10-Q shows the means to ship more: customer deposits rose from $78.2M at 12/31/25 to $360.6M at 6/30/26, total deferred revenue plus deposits from $143.8M to $445.0M, inventory to $758.2M (finished goods $224.0M), and product/installation RPO to $442.4M from $394.4M. Expect a revenue beat of about 3% (~$1.10B).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (rev $1,065M vs ~$0.96-1.0B bar, raise) closed -1.85% close-to-close after +12% after hours. Q1 2026 (rev $751M, big beat and raise) +27.2%. Q3 2025 +18.0%. Q2 2025 -1.79%. The response to beats is mixed and was sold last time.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has been unchanged for 60 days (Zacks), so the Street has not modelled sequential growth into Q3. Zacks ESP is -5.63%, meaning the most recent estimates sit below consensus. If the market priced a beat, the bar would have drifted up and the stock would not be down 23% in 20 sessions.
findings.independence: The track record of 7 of 8 beats is from a separate source (TradingView/SA, https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:c7e3e76f0094b:0-bloom-energy-s-q3-results-to-test-ai-driven-growth-expectations/). The deposit and inventory figures share the 10-Q document.

findings.finding: FY2026 guide ($3.9-4.2B revenue) has been raised at both prior prints (Q1 from about 60% growth to 80%, Q2 to about 100%). The CFO cited 'visibility and confidence we have for our second half', and the CEO said the 2026 guide has no dependence on any single project. Consensus sits only about 1.5% above the midpoint, so a third raise to around $4.2B+ is the base case. The bar for a positive reaction is probably above the published consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 raise (+$0.6B at midpoint) +27.2%. Q2 2026 raise (+$0.45B at midpoint) -1.85% close-to-close despite +12% after hours.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a raise is expected. FY consensus at only +1.5% over the midpoint (Trefis 2026-10-14) means a raise to the top end or above is not fully in the published numbers. The 21% one-week drawdown shows the market fears a guide cut tied to Jupiter.
findings.independence: The FY consensus-vs-midpoint figure is from Trefis (https://www.trefis.com/articles/618686/what-are-bloom-energy-investors-betting-on/2026-10-14), a separate source. The guide itself is the company's 8-K.

findings.finding: Oracle's Project Jupiter (New Mexico, ~2.4-2.45 GW of Bloom fuel cells) is under a force majeure notice (2026-09-24) and its gas pipeline has slipped to 2027-02-01. On 2026-10-15 Oracle/Yucca offered an enforceable cap on fuel-cell operating output to cut permitted emissions ~35%, and the air permit is still pending. Enverus estimates Jupiter plus its option is nearly half of Bloom's product backlog. The call will be asked whether Jupiter shipments or bookings shift out of 2026/2027; that risks the 2027 narrative even if the 2026 guide holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the 9/24 force majeure news BE fell ~3-5% intraday, then rebounded +8% on Bloom/Oracle reaffirmation. The 10/9-10/16 slide of -21% was attributed partly to Jupiter. There is no print-day history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is -21% in a week with Jupiter named as the company-specific cause. What is not priced is management's answer on the call: any shift of delivery or recognition timing, or any reduced installed MW under the output cap, has not been disclosed by Bloom. The mild skew (+2 vol points) says the options market does not see a large asymmetric downside.
findings.independence: Force majeure and the 2027-02-01 pipeline slip: CNBC https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/oracle-data-center-force-majeure.html. The output cap: Microgrid Knowledge 2026-10-20 https://www.microgridknowledge.com/data-center-microgrids/news/55413142/oracle-promises-ai-enabled-project-jupiter-fuel-cell-emissions-refined-35-lower. Net of the rest: the CEO said the 2026 guide does not depend on any single project, and Oracle's wider 2.8 GW partnership (1.2 GW contracted, deploying) plus AEP/Brookfield sit outside Jupiter.

findings.finding: Revenue concentration is extreme. The 10-Q/A (filed 2026-07-29 to correct swapped periods) shows one non-related-party customer at ~73% of Q2 revenue and AR concentrations of 36%/34%/17%. The CFO: 'one or two customers could lead our revenue in any given quarter.' Any Q3 timing slip at that customer moves the quarter by hundreds of millions either way, and it raises the Q&A and quality-of-revenue scrutiny Roth has flagged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Concentration was disclosed with Q2, after which the stock closed -1.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed only in the 10-Q/A footnote, not in the release or the previews. Previews anchor on $1.07B without discussing that one customer's delivery timing sets the quarter. Mostly a variance driver, so it is sized small negative.
findings.independence: Magica commentary on the concentration test: https://magica.com/news/bloom-energy-ai-power-forecast-concentration-test. It shares the same 10-Q/A underlying fact.

findings.finding: Counterparty demand signal: Oracle's FQ1 FY27 (reported 2026-09-10, after Bloom last spoke) shows 850 MW of data-center capacity delivered in the quarter, 'approaching one gigawatt' per quarter, FY27 capex guided to $90-95B, and RPO of $664B. Oracle is Bloom's largest AI customer (up to 2.8 GW partnership).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for six weeks, so mostly priced. It is a proxy: Oracle did not name Bloom. The stock has fallen since, on AI-infrastructure financing worries (Oracle -7% on capex), so the market reads Oracle capex as a risk rather than as Bloom demand.
findings.independence: Oracle 2.8 GW partnership, 1.2 GW contracted and deploying: https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-and-Oracle-Expand-Strategic-Partnership-to-Deploy-up-to-2-8-GW-to-Accelerate-AI-Infrastructure-Build-Out/default.aspx

findings.finding: On 2026-10-14 AEP announced a $4B, 702 MW Bloom fuel-cell plant in Wyoming under a 20-year Google PPA, with construction starting in 2026 and fully operational by end-2028. It is supplied under Bloom's existing up-to-1 GW AEP agreement, which converts framework capacity into a named, financed project that can enter Q3/Q4 bookings or backlog commentary. The same day AEP bought 190 MW of Mainspring linear generators (up to 1.6 GW), a competing on-site technology.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on prints. The stock fell through the week of the announcement.
findings.why_not_priced: Announced by AEP, not Bloom, and it lands after the Q3 close. Previews do not quantify what it adds to bookings. Any backlog or bookings number on the call is the first place it shows. The Mainspring order is a small offset.
findings.independence: Power Magazine on the AEP/Mainspring and Bloom plan: https://www.powermag.com/aep-plans-4-billion-fuel-cell-power-plant-for-google-signs-up-to-1-6-gw-mainspring-generator-deal/

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out rather than crowded. The stock is -22.7% over 20 days, -11.1% over 5, -38.5% off its high, and about -10% on the print day itself. Short interest is only 7.3% of float with 1.0 days to cover. The Street mean target is ~$285-297 against ~$213 spot, and EPS estimates were revised up 17 times and down 0 times in three months. An in-line quarter with a held or raised guide meets a lowered price bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the stock fell 11.3% on print day before the release and then closed -1.85% the next day, so a print-day selloff did not set up a bounce last time.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the price. The question is whether it overshoots the Jupiter risk. A straddle of 10% with only +2 skew says the market is not paying up for a further collapse. A broad tech selloff (Nasdaq 100 -2.75% today) adds macro beta to the next session in either direction.
findings.independence: Short interest: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/BE/short-interest/. Price drop and targets: TIKR https://www.tikr.com/blog/bloom-energy-stock-fell-21-in-a-week-heres-what-its-october-22-report-needs-to-show

findings.finding: Insider selling cluster since the Q2 print: EDGAR shows about 13 Form 144 proposed-sale notices and about 16 Form 4s between 2026-07-01 and 2026-10-02, including four Form 144s on 2026-09-16 and one on 2026-10-01. No insider purchases are visible.
findings.why_not_priced: Public filings that are likely 10b5-1 plan sales after a 170%+ YTD run. It is weak signal, sized small.

findings.finding: Short-seller overhang: Hunterbrook published reports on 2026-07-08 (scandium oxide supply from China) and 2026-08-03 (fuel-cell efficiency and lifespan). Bloom rebutted the first in an 8-K (item 7.01, 2026-07-09) and class actions followed. Q&A on supply chain or revenue quality is likely, and Roth flagged transparency.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-08 report caused a -12% day. The Q2 print three weeks later closed -1.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, three months old. It is filed because a clean quarter with strong cash flow (CFO baseline: operating cash flow of $375M+) would rebut it, and a working-capital or receivables blowout would revive it.

outside_window.finding: Project Jupiter: hearing on New Energy Economy's motion to dismiss the air-permit application is set for 2026-10-26, and the NMED air-permit decision is due 2026-11-23. Both are binary for roughly half of Bloom's backlog (Enverus estimate).

searched_and_found_nothing: No Bloom 8-K or press release since 2026-07-28 other than the 2026-10-12 date notice and the 2026-07-09 Hunterbrook rebuttal (EDGAR filing list), so no in-quarter pre-announcement.
Vertiv and GE Vernova Q3 2026 results were not yet indexed, so no peer print after Bloom last spoke was found apart from Oracle FQ1.
No disclosed backlog dollar figure; the Q2 call gave only 'backlog growing faster than revenue'.
No Hunterbrook follow-up dated September or October 2026 found.
No current hiring or capacity-expansion data checked beyond the company statements.

baseline_tension: The slight long lean cuts against the mild downside skew (+2.06) and the momentum of a -23% 20-day run-up. It agrees with the free control (-run_up_20d), which says buy the drawdown. The Q2 precedent of a beat and raise being sold keeps p_up at 55, not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the reported-quarter beat finding was cut from +1.5 to +1.0, because the Q2 beat and raise closed -1.85%.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): the Oracle capex counterparty proxy was cut from +0.5 to +0.4.
Lessons 1 and 7 together: the positioning/washed-out finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.8, because the Q2 print-day selloff did not produce a bounce.

Lesson 6: bar verified against four agreeing sources ($1.07B); the Jupiter permit dates (10-26, 11-23) were already in outside_window. Lesson 9: Jupiter is sized net of the CEO's statement that the 2026 guide is not single-project dependent, so it was left at -1.5.
